newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/4, but activity light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- up 1/4, but activity light.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds gained 1/4 point Friday, but proof of the improvement was hard to find in the form of actual trades.
Traders said activity was extremely light, but judged secondary prices higher based on stronger Treasury and futures markets.
The government market held on to gains scored after a favorable producer price report for June.
The Labor Department reported early in the day that June producer prices fell 0.1 percent overall and rose 0.1 percent when food and energy prices were excluded.
Analysts, who were expecting an unchanged overall rate, said the figure meant that the Federal Reserve was unlikely to raise interest rates again soon.
The long bond was up 15/32 at 101-8/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
In the muni secondary market, Allegheny County Sanitary Authority Pa., MBIA 5-3/8s of 2024 were bid at 5.51 percent, down one basis point from the close on Thursday.
Florida Ports Financing Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2027 were unchanged at 5.55 percent.
In futures, the September municipal contract closed up 5/32 at 119-16/32, while September T-bonds gained 8/32 to 114-4/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 172 from 175 at the close on Thursday.
Municipal bond sales for next week were expected to total $2.507 billion in 122 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.780 billion in 47 sales, with a $350 million Los Angeles Unified School District offering through BancAmerica topping the list.
On the competitive side, 75 sales totaling $727 million are scheduled. A $78.5 million Virginia HDA offering on July 17 is the largest competitive offering.
